story:
The Adamsons are a family of clerks. Gracien Adamson keeps the register of names at Fort Gwyntell in the Dales, and a second book besides, of the dales' dead who still give their names. His cousin Tristram came to Caldey in the first year of the war to keep the accounts of the colleges' burying isle, and was in Little Haven when the isle stood up, and stayed. The cousins write to each other. Gracien's letters are about names. Tristram's are about bones.

The ebon skeletons are the worst of Caldey's walking dead for one reason: they walk off the isle. The black dead of the deep graves go down into the water on the eastern strand and come up again on the Isle of Glass, under the wall of Caer Gothwaite, and the garrison there has buried them a second time more often than it likes. Tristram worked out why they reach it and the others do not. They walk the whole way, under the sea, on the bottom. A skeleton that walks needs its legs; a skeleton without a shin-bone does not walk anywhere. So he pays for shin-bones. He has done the reckoning on the back of the ledger: so many tibias paid for, so many fewer at the Gothwaite wall, and he sends the reckoning to the garrison every quarter and the garrison sends back a thank-you and a complaint.

He keeps the bones in a shed behind his house, two to a skeleton, and writes them up as his cousin writes up names: one column for what came in, one for what he can prove will never walk again. The second column is the longer. He says that is the difference between his book and Gracien's. Gracien can never prove anybody is dead. Tristram can always prove a skeleton is lame.

He has never harmed anyone; he is a clerk. The clan's defenders count him among the outpost's own, and would come down off the wall for him, he says, though he hopes never to find out.
legend: Tristram Adamson is a level 54 villager of Little Haven on Caldey who buys Rotted Ebon Skeleton Tibias (his turn-in, levels 48 to 49). He is not hostile: the Caldey Outpost faction starts neutral, and he leaves players of his quest's level band alone. Killing him brings the clan's barbarian defenders (same faction) and sours your standing with the outpost; there is no quest for it. No spells or styles in the data. The ebon skeletons whose shin-bones he wants walk Caldey itself, and his turn-in pays well for its level band. The other Little Haven buyers (Rose, Huidelon Cariston, Waleron Douglas) stand close by.

loremasterTopic.text: A clerk of [little haven], cousin to Gracien Adamson the registrar of Fort Gwyntell. He pays for the shin-bones of the ebon skeletons, because they walk off [caldey] under the sea to the wall of Caer Gothwaite, and a skeleton without a shin walks nowhere. He sends the garrison his reckoning every quarter. He keeps the bones two to a skeleton, in a shed.

bookPage: Tristram Adamson of Little Haven, to his cousin Gracien Adamson, registrar of Fort Gwyntell. Cousin: your last letter asks how I can be sure the skeletons whose shins I have bought will not walk again. I am not sure they are dead. Nobody on this isle is. I am sure they are lame. You keep a book in which nothing can be proved, and I keep one in which everything can, and I think we are both doing the same work: writing down what the war cannot take back. This quarter, one hundred and twelve shins, fifty-six skeletons. The garrison at the wall writes that it has buried eleven fewer. They also write that the smell from my shed reaches them across the water. That is untrue, but I have entered it.
